question.problem:
The Sun has a mass of $(1.99\times {10}^{30})\,\text{kg}$ and Jupiter has a mass of $(1.90\times {10}^{27})\,\text{kg}.$
The average distance between the centers of the Sun and Jupiter is $(7.78\times {10}^{11})\,\text{m}.$ According to Newton's law of universal gravitation, what is the magnitude of the gravitational force between the Sun and Jupiter? Write your answer in scientific notation, rounding to **three significant figures** where appropriate. Assume the Newtonian constant of gravitation is $G=(6.67\times {10}^{-11})\,{\text{m}}^{3}/(\text{kg}\cdot {\text{s}}^{2}).$

The magnitude of the force between the Sun and Jupiter is
$(${{field-1}}
$\times $
{{field-2}}$)\,\text{N}.$
question.worked_solution:
Newton's law of universal gravitation states that the gravitational force attracting two objects is proportional to the product of the two masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers of mass:

$$
F=G\frac{{m}_{1}{m}_{2}}{{r}^{2}}
$$

where

- $F$ is the gravitational force between the objects, measured in Newtons $(\text{N}),$

- $G=(6.67\times {10}^{-11})\,{\text{m}}^{3}/(\text{kg}\cdot {\text{s}}^{2})$ is the Newtonian constant of gravitation,

- ${m}_{1}$ and ${m}_{2}$ are the masses of the objects, measured in $\text{kg},$ and

- $r$ is the distance between their centers of mass, measured in $\text{m}.$

Let ${m}_{1}$ be the mass of the Sun and ${m}_{2}$ be the mass of Jupiter. Then, substituting in the known values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =(6.67\times {10}^{-11})\cdot \frac{(1.99\times {10}^{30})\cdot (1.90\times {10}^{27})}{(7.78\times {10}^{11})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6.67\cdot 1.99\cdot 1.90}{(7.78)^{2}}\times \frac{{10}^{-11}\cdot {10}^{30}\cdot {10}^{27}}{({10}^{11})^{2}} \\  & =(0.416\,651…)\times {10}^{24} \\  & =(4.166\,51…)\times {10}^{23}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, rounded to three significant figures, the gravitational force between the Sun and Jupiter is
$(\,4.17\times {10}^{23}\,)\,\text{N}.$
